Haleshū anil veyherub.
(Let it depart from him and flee.)

— and also write the name of the illness you wish him to be afflicted with. Then nail the pitch to the ground at its four corners, or fix it to the wall on the east side of the house. After that, fumigate with coriander and myrrh incense and continue reciting the asmāʾ al-[I 419] Barhatiyya; if you continue this recitation, the oppressive enemy will, in the shortest time, be afflicted with the torment and illness you have written.

4×4 number wafq of the divine name Berheyūlā, written to recover lost or stolen property — the frame names the four archangels: Gabriel [Jibrīl] above; ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl] right; Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl] below; Michael [Mīkāʾīl] left; talismanic cipher marks at the four corners. [I 419]
The fifteenth name is Berheyula; its letter is Sin (2) and its lunar mansion is Ghafir. Its Arabic equivalent: Subhanallah enallahu haifine Ya Kafi Ya Semiu Ya Allahu ruhi li ruhike muntesi betun.
(Glory be to God — surely God is the One who is to be feared. O Sufficient One, O All-Hearing One, O God, my spirit is affiliated to Your Spirit.)
These are its noble names. This noble name was the litany of Abraham (peace be upon him); with this noble name he glorified and remembered the Creator of the universe. The khawāṣṣof this name are:

To find something lost: If a person who has lost something writes this noble name's fourfold wafq — and around the wafq writes the noble name Berheyūlā seven times — and this wafq is then hung in the house where the item was lost, the lost or stolen property will be found by God's leave.

To see what you wish for in a dream: If you want to see something you desire in your dream, after performing a thorough ablution, for the sake of God's pleasure — [I 420] you perform a six-rak'ah prayer of need (ḥāja namazi), giving the greeting of peace at the end of every two rak'ahs.
After the prayer, write the name Barheyula seven times on your right palm and say the following:
Naming your wish in place of "such-and-such," whatever it may be, then lying down to sleep, you will see what you desire.
Bashkaylahin
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 420
The sixteenth name is Bashkaylahin; its letter is ayn (1) and its lunar mansion (manzil, one of the twenty-eight stations of the moon) is Zebane. Its Arabic equivalent is:
(O Believer! Might belongs to Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful.)
— these are its noble names. The exalted properties (khawāṣṣ) of this blessed name are:
For eye pain: On a Monday, write this name seven times on a piece of paper, and the following verses once:
By him I sought refuge when grief touched him — the shirt of) Yūsuf, when the bearer of good news brought it. By the right of (!Ya'kūb, O eye-pain, depart
[I 421] After writing it, if the person whose eyes ache carries it upon his head, he is freed from the eye pain.
For distress and stress: If a person in distress and under stress continues to recite this noble name seventy times every night, he will be freed from his troubles and distress in a short time.
Qazmazin
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 421
The seventeenth name is Qazmazin; its letter is fā (8) and its lunar mansion is Iklīl. Its Arabic equivalent is:
(O Guardian, through the might of Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful.)

3×3 number wafq of the divine name al-Ghanī [Ghanī], written for abundance — the frame names the four archangels: Gabriel [Jibrīl] above; ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl] right; Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl] below; Michael [Mīkāʾīl] left; cipher marks at the four corners. [I 421]
— these are its noble names. This noble name is the glorification recited by Jesus, peace be upon him. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:

For abundance (baraka): On a new piece of blue silk, write this noble name together with the threefold wafq of the name Ghani, "the All-Sufficient." After writing it, place the inscribed silk inside a purse whose contents are of unknown amount, hang the purse from a blackberry-bramble rod, and, fuming it with raw amber and musk incense (bakhūr), recite the Barhatiyya names one hundred times on Friday night; you will see abundance descend upon it. If this purse is used like a wallet, you will find that your money never runs out.

[I 422] For protection from an enemy: Whoever wishes to be protected from an enemy's evil and to prevail over him should invoke the names Beshkaylehin and Qazmazin frequently; he will be protected from the enemy's evil and will prevail.
The eighteenth name is Enghalelitin; its letter is sād (7) and its lunar mansion is Kalb. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its noble names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:

To make someone depart: Write this noble name on a piece of unfired pottery together with Sūrat al-Fīl (the Chapter of the Elephant), then pound the piece thoroughly and grind it to powder. If this powder is scattered at the home of the enemy troubling you, he will leave that place at once.
To extinguish a fire: Whoever recites this noble name often, if he recites it facing a fire and wishes for the fire to go out, the fire will be extinguished before it can spread.

For an apparition: Write this noble name on a plate, wash off the writing with water, and if this water is sprinkled in a place where an apparition has been seen, no apparition will ever be seen there again.
The nineteenth name is Kabarātin; its letter is kāf (6) and its lunar mansion is Shūle. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its noble names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
[I 423] To be safe from illnesses: Write this noble name on a piece of paper together with the following verse (Āyāt al-Karima):
.In the name of Allah, the Compassionate, the Merciful (Today We shall deliver you in your body, that you may be a sign to" those who come after you." And indeed, many among mankind ..are.)
After writing it, whoever carries it upon himself will not be afflicted by plague or other contagious diseases, and his enemies will be unable to harm him either.

To never encounter what one dislikes: Whoever makes a habit (wird) of reciting this noble name sixty times every day will, by the permission of Allah Almighty, never encounter anything displeasing or unwelcome to him.
The twentieth name is Ghayaha; its letter is rā (5) and its lunar mansion is Nuaym. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
To stop bleeding: Write this noble name ninety times — thirty at a time, over three sittings — on a red piece of paper, together with the following verse:
(In the name of Allah, the

Compassionate, the Merciful. Indeed, He is truly able to bring it back.) written as detached letters (ḥurūf-u mukattaa, the disjointed Arabic letters), then, after washing off the writing with water, if this water is given to drink to a woman whose menstrual bleeding will not stop, her bleeding will cease by the permission of Allah Almighty.
[I 424] The twenty-first name is Keydehula; its letter is shīn (<) and its lunar mansion is Belde. Its Arabic equivalent — these are its noble names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
To nullify sorcery: On a piece of paper, draw the following seal (khātam, a talismanic seal):

3×3 seal [khātam] of the divine name Keydehūlā, written to undo sorcery, its cells filled with three repeating cipher glyphs — frame: Gabriel [Jibrīl] above; ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl] right; Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl] below; Michael [Mīkāʾīl] left. [I 424]
Around the seal, write the name Keydehūlā one hundred (100) times, and, written as detached letters, the following verses once (1).
In the name of Allah, the)

Compassionate, the Merciful. "And throw down what is in your right hand; it will swallow up what they have made. What they have made is only a magician's trick, and the magician will not succeed ,wherever he goes. And Allah establishes the truth by His words (".even though the guilty detest it

[I 425] After writing it, whoever carries this amulet (ḥirz) upon himself will not be seized by sorcery; if sorcery has already been cast upon him, it will be nullified, and he will attain healing by the permission of Allah the Exalted.

Whoever continually recites the names Kabaratin and Ghayaha over someone afflicted by the evil eye (naẓar), or directs them toward the eyes of his enemies, blinds his enemies' eyes — his enemies lose the power of sight at that very moment and cannot see him.

To attain high ranks: Whoever wishes to reach the ranks attained by the blessed masters and achieve complete spiritual union (vuslat), let him enter spiritual retreat (khalwa), observing its conditions, and recite the names Ghayāhan and Keydehūlā frequently, reciting the Tījan names — the "crown" names — once at the end of every hundred repetitions; his wish will be granted by the permission of Allah the Exalted.
The Tījan names are these:
I 426] Shamhāhirin The twenty-second]
name is Shamhāhirin; its letter is tā (;) and its lunar mansion is Sa'd :al-Zābih. Its Arabic equivalent is
Tealeyte Ya Aliyyu Ya Alimu (You are exalted, O Most High, O All-Knowing.)
— these are its names. The exalted properties of this name are:

To drive away ants: Write this noble name seven (7) times on a clean plate, then wash off the writing with spring water; if this water is sprinkled where there are ants, the ants will leave that place and, by the permission of Allah Almighty, will never be seen there again.
Shamhāhirin
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 426
The twenty-third name is Shamhāhirin; its letter is se (:) and its lunar mansion is Sa'd al-Bula'. Its Arabic equivalent is:
Ya Kadi Ya Hu Ya Hu Ya Rabbahu Ya Rabbahu (O Judge, O He, O He, O my Lord, O my Lord.)
— these are its names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
In a place where mosquitoes are plentiful, if this noble name is written fifteen (15) times on a piece of paper and then burned there, the mosquitoes will flee from that place.

[I 427] The twenty-fourth name is Shemhāhīrin; its letter is khāʾ (9) and its lunar mansion is Sa'd al-Water'ūd. Its Arabic meaning — these are its names. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
To separate two people: Write this noble name one hundred (100) times on a piece of paper, and then once the following verse:
And We have cast)
—enmity and hatred between them until the Day of Resurrection (.between so-and-so, son of so-and-so
Write it with the name of the person you wish to part, then bury it at the place where those who need to be separated from each other reside; they will part from one another as enemies.
For lovesickness (kara sevda, an obsessive melancholic longing): Write this noble name seven (7) times on a plate, and the following verse three (3) times:
(And indeed, We made a covenant with

Adam before, but he forgot.) After writing it together with the name of the petitioner and his mother's name, wash off the writing with water; if the petitioner drinks this water on an empty stomach, he will forget the one he loves, come to feel aversion toward them, and be delivered from this affliction of lovesickness.
If, while performing a working (amal, a magical operation), you wish to know whether the spirits have come, recite the names Shamhāhirin and
Shemhehirin one hundred (100) times,
(O Spirits! If you have come, show me a light from your radiance.)
[I 428] and after reciting it say, "O Spirits! If you have come, show me a light from your radiance" — a light like sunlight will shine where you are.

The twenty-fifth name is Bikehtahūnīhin; its letter is dhāl (@) and its lunar mansion is Sa'd al-Ahbiya. Its Arabic meaning — these are its names. Of the four additional names appended by the scholars, the first is Bikehtahunihin, which some have also called Bikehtunihin, others Bikehtahtunihin, and others still Bikehtahtahunihin. According to the consensus of the scholars, the correct one is the first name. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:

To never feel hunger: Write this noble name seventy (70) times on a clean plate, wash off the writing with water, and whoever drinks this water on an empty stomach in the morning will, by the permission of Allah Almighty, never feel hunger.
The twenty-sixth name is Besharishin; its letter is dād (?) and its lunar mansion is al-Fer' al-Muqaddam. Its Arabic meaning is:
Yā kādiran ʿalā kulli shayʾin (O He who has power over all things.)
— these are its names. The name Beshārishin has also been called Sharishin. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:

[I 429] To never suffer thirst: Whoever recites this noble name countless times, again and again, will not suffer thirst. His spirit attains purity and he is cleansed of carnal impulses. Wise words pour forth from his tongue.

The twenty-seventh name is Tūneshin; its letter is ẓāʾ (>) and its lunar mansion is al-Fer' al-Mu'ahhar. Its Arabic meaning — these are its names. The scholars of the science of khawāṣṣ (occult properties) have also called the name Tūneshin by Tūshin, Tarshin, or Tūyāshin. According to the consensus of the scholars, the correct noble name is Tūneshin. The exalted properties of this blessed name are:
For a crying child: draw the following fourfold wafq of this noble name:
After writing Sūrat al-Fātiḥa eleven (11) times around the wafq, if this amulet is fastened upon the crying child, the child's crying will stop by the permission of Allah the Exalted.

For a wish: Whoever has a request to make of Allah the Exalted should, after the night prayer, perform a two-rak'ah prayer of need for that request from Allah, in the final prostration of the second rak'ah, raising his head from the prostration

4×4 letter wafq of the divine name Tūneshin, worn as an amulet to quiet a crying child — frame: Gabriel [Jibrīl] above; ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl] right; Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl] below; Michael [Mīkāʾīl] left; cipher marks at the corners. [I 429]
[I 430] without lifting [the pen], reading it eighty (80) times, and asking one's wish from Allah Ta'ala, the wish is granted.

For headache: after writing this noble name on a piece of paper twenty (20) times — and the letter sat (7), too, ninety (90) times — if the person suffering the headache carries this ḥirz (protective amulet) upon them, by the permission of Allah Ta'ala they will be relieved of the headache.

The properties of the name Tuyashin are like the properties of the name Tuneshin. The wafq of the name Tuyashin is a five-by-five wafq. I have not dwelt on the properties of the names Tarashin and Tushin, nor on the meaning of the other narrations.

The twenty-eighth name is Shemhābārūhin, whose letter is (=) and whose manzil (lunar mansion) is Resha. Its meaning in Arabic is: [it is one of the] Names. The exalted khawāṣṣ (occult properties) of this blessed name are:
To break sorcery: write this noble name on a plate together with this noble verse (aya-i Karima):
Ji'tum bihis sihru
(What you have brought is sorcery; Allah will surely bring it to nothing. Indeed, Allah does not set right the work of those who spread corruption.)
After writing it, wash the writing off with water, and if you give this water to the bewitched person to drink, by the permission of Allah (c.c.)
they will be freed from the sorcery.
For a wish or a need: if you have a request or a wish concerning someone, after reciting Surah Yā-Sīn once and this noble name thirty-five (35)
times, if you then ask that person for your wish and your need, by the permission of Allah (c.c.) what you wished for will come to pass.
For healing: if you write this noble name for someone who is sick, bound (under a spell), or bewitched, and the sick person carries this writing upon them, they will find healing.

[I 431] To triumph over an enemy: if you write the whole of the Barhatiyya names upon a weapon and go before your enemy, you will prevail over them. They will not be able to stand before you, and they will flee.

Whatever kind of wish a person has, take the letters of the talib (the petitioner), the maṭlūb (the object of the working), and the wish itself, and add them together according to the abjad (the numerical alphabet).
Then subtract 28 from the total, again and again. Whichever asmāʾ (name)
the remainder corresponds to, take that name's letter, and write the name on a piece of paper as many times as the numerical value of that letter.

After writing it, recite the name over it as many times as its numerical value — but you must do this on the name's night and in its manzil (lunar mansion). After that, subtract 4 from the total again and again, and act, according to the remaining number, in keeping with the ʿanāṣir-i arbaʿa (the four elements). If the remainder is one, its element is fire:

you burn what you wrote in fire, or bury it beneath the fire. If it is two, its element is earth: you bury what you wrote at the threshold of the maṭlūb, in the ground, or in a grave. If it is three, its element is air: you hang what you wrote up facing the wind, or carry it on your person. If it is four, its element is earth: if you give the water [used to wash off] what you wrote to the maṭlūb to drink, or bury it beneath running water, what you wished for comes to pass.

For example: the talib's name is Ali, whose value is 110; the maṭlūb's name is Zeyneb, whose value is 69; our wish is mahabba (love), whose value is 450. We added the three together and the total came to 629. We subtracted 28 from this number again and again, and 22 remained.

The twenty-second (22) name, Shamhāhirin, has the letter Te, whose value is 400. We write the name Shamhāhirin on a piece of paper 400 times, and we recite the name Shamhāhirin over it 1146 times. After that we subtract 4 from 629 again and again, and since one (1) remains, its element is fire: we burn the paper we wrote in fire, or bury it beneath the fire.
But we perform this working only when the Moon (Qamar) spends the night in the manzil of Sa'du'z-Zabih.

If you wish to use the Barhatiyya Qasam and make it your own: for the sake of Allah's pleasure (Allah, c.c. — celle jelāluhū, "exalted is His majesty") fast for seven (7) days in ascetic discipline (riyada). Each day, write out the complete set of twenty-eight Barhatiyya names on a china plate with rosewater, musk, and saffron; then wash the writing off with spring water, and break your fast with that water. After breaking your fast, eat unsalted barley bread and unsalted olive oil. Recite the Asmāʾ al-Barhatiyya Qasam forty-five (45) times after every obligatory prayer, and perfume the place where you are with Ummal bakhūr (incense) —

henna-flower seed. Once you have completed the seven days in this way, you gain the right to use the Barhatiyya for whatever you wish. From then on, you will use the following buhurs for workings of good or of ill.
On Sunday, for workings of good: use Meyatu Saile, Kundur (frankincense), and henna-flower bakhūr.
On Monday: Ned (aloeswood) twig, Mastaki (mastic), Sakiz (gum mastic), and Samk-i Arabi (gum arabic).
On Tuesday: Sandali Ahmer (red sandalwood), Senderus (sandarac resin), and Kundur.
On Wednesday: Mastaki and Karanfil (clove).
On Thursday: Cavi (benzoin).
On Friday: Ned twig and Shebb-i Yemani (Yemeni alum).
On Saturday: Udu Hindi (Indian aloeswood) and Sezab (rue) root.
On Sunday, for workings of ill: Ṣabr (aloe resin), Murre (myrrh), and Muklil Erzak (bdellium).
On Monday: Ṣabr, Murre, and Haltit (asafoetida).
On Tuesday: Muklil Erzak and Meyatu Saile.

On Friday: Sumak (sumac) and Udu Salip.
On Saturday: white pepper and eggshell — these are the buhurs you use.

On the sick person's forehead, write this figure: on his right hand, He Mīm; on his left hand, Ye ʿAyn; on the back of his right foot, certain letters; and on the back of his left foot, Sat Qāf — write these letters. Afterward, recite the Qasam until the jinn inside the sick person asks for help and says it wishes to leave. If the possessing jinn says it wishes to leave, erase the letters on the sick person's left foot, and the possessing jinn will leave and never return to that person again.
58. If you wish to perform a jinn-summoning: take the abjad value, 3866, of this verse:
(And thus We showed Abraham the kingdom of the heavens and the earth, that he might be of those who are certain.)
[I 474] and make a threefold wafq with it. On the four sides of the wafq write this name:

Kawfu Above this name write the names of the four great angels; above the angels, the names of the four caliphs. Write all of this on a white porcelain plate. Afterward, put olive oil in the plate and have a young child born under an air sign gaze into it. Recite Surah ash-Shams together with the Qasam until the khuddām arrive. When they arrive, tell them to sweep, sprinkle water, lay out the rugs and chairs, and do the other familiar things.
The form of the wafq to be written is this:

3×3 numerical wafq framed by three tiers of names on each side — outermost the four caliphs (Abu Bakr above, Umar left, Ali right, Uthman below), then the archangels Gabriel, Michael, ʿAzrāʾīl and Isrāfīl, and nearest the square the name Kawfu. [I 474]

Seal of Ehcezet [Echezetin hatemi], for sickening a tyrant — five Arabic letters set in a cross; above them, "take charge, O servants" [tewekkelū yā huddām]; at the left, "this is the wafq"; the whole enclosed in a hooked ornamental border. [I 475]
[I 475] But when performing this working you must fast that day and observe riyada (ascetic discipline). Reflect! By God's leave and grace, glory be to Him, you will find the right path.

3×3 wafq of the divine name Allah in the archangel frame — Gabriel [Jibrīl] above; Michael [Mīkāʾīl] left; ʿAzrāʾīl [ʿAzrāʾīl] right; Isrāfīl [Isrāfīl] below; corner letters; the lower middle cell is marked "request" [ḥāja], where the petitioner writes his wish. [I 475]
If you wish to make a tyrannical oppressor ill

60. If you wish for someone afflicted by a spiritual illness to be healed: write the Qasam on a white plate with musk, saffron, and rosewater. Afterward, recite the Qasam over it seven (7) times, wash the writing off with water, and if you give this water to the sick person to drink, God willing, glory be to Him, he will be healed.

61. For an important and weighty request: this threefold wafq of the name Allah, [I 476] on a sheet of paper, and in the wafq's empty cell write your request. Afterward, beginning on a Sunday, enter khalwa (spiritual seclusion) and, observing riyada, fast for seven (7) days. Recite the noble name of Allah 66,000 times each day, and at the end of every thousand (1000) recitations, recite the Barhatiyya names up to Bashkaylahin three (3) times. After completing the seven days, place the wafq you have written beneath the prayer rug on which you sit, and if you recite the noble name Dhāt (Allah) 1,000 times and the Barhatiyya names three (3) times, the request you have made will be granted swiftly, in the shortest time.
If you wish to bring about any request, benevolent or malevolent
63. If you wish to attract good and repel evil: write this threefold wafq of the name Semi' (the All-Hearing), and in the center of the wafq write your request:
[I 477] After writing it, perform a two-rak'ah prayer of need (ḥāja namazi). After the Fātiḥa, recite the Surah al-Ikhlāṣfive times. After the prayer, recite this noble verse:
(In the name of

Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Our Lord, accept this from us; indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing.) —180 times; then the Qasam (the Oath, a set invocatory formula) 41 times; then the noble name Yā Semī' 180 times. Once you have recited these, you then recite the following blessed prayer seven times:
besheriyeti ven

,O Allah, I ask of You, O All-Hearing (by Your Name that hears — the Name that has spread out the wonders of the resting-places of the souls that carry the divine secrets, through the vessels that bear the lordly words — a pure acceptance, untouched by the veil of human weakness and ,unclouded by the darkness of the dense fogs of the carnal self before which the divine self-disclosures shine forth; a Name for which You have made the vessels of the heart the suns of the lights of the unseen, rising up from the horizons of witnessing, so that they roam free in the noble gardens and wade through the meadows in the ancient orchards, neither grieving over what has passed nor rejoicing over what is yet to come. Glory be to You, O Allah — how generous is Your generosity, how exalted is Your mercy above all mercy! You have made the gardens of Your generosity and mercy laugh with the dawn of the felicitous, so that the hearts of Your saints may pluck their fruit with the fingers of Your favor. I ask You, O Allah, by what You have deposited in this great prayer of Your hidden secrets and stored-up lights, to immerse me in the ocean of Your generosity and mercy, and to grant me mastery over the reins of Your bounty and grace, until the hardest of affairs become tractable to me and the wonders of such-and-such are unveiled to me, by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.)
If you wish, you may also recite this prayer before the noble verse.
[I 479] Once you have completed the working, take the wafq with you and turn toward the object of your need (ḥāja); by Allah's leave, your need will surely be met.

Know this: whoever performs this while fasting, in ascetic discipline (riyada), and in a righteous spiritual retreat (khalwa) holds the reins of every working in his hand. He will attain a lofty rank in the eyes of all people.
If you wish to perform the dismissal of the indwelling spirits (sarf al-ummar), you say the following seven times:

A conjuration calling (upon the Most High above His throne, and calling to Gabriel to descend to the earth and cry out a shattering torment there, so that — the jinn scatter east and west — beings of fire and brass commanding them to depart at once, by the might of a long chain of potent names, each repeated twice, and finally invoking God's might: unless You have seized their hearing and their sight. Glory be to Him who has no likeness — He is the Hearing, the Seeing.)

For love (mahabba), write the following Mufradāt (Singular) and Muzdawijāt (Paired) awfāq — the Mufradāt wafq for the maṭlūb (the object of the working, the person desired), and the Muzdawijāt wafq for the talib (the seeker, the one who desires)
The Tījān Invocation (Tījān Daʿwa)

[I 485] Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm Allāhumma Ya Beshmehin Dalaha Musheytishshun. Ya Allahun nafizu emruhu. Ellezi lehul asmāʾ-ul Husna ves sifatul ulya wa-l- behjetu ved diya-u ven nuru wa-l- behau.

— He from whom no hidden thing is concealed, nor what breasts keep secret.) Allāhumma Ya Seyhusimin Zarishin Erkashin Dare Aliyyun.

(O Allah, the All-Knowing, the Knower — He whose command, when He wills a thing, is only to say to it "Be," and it is. So glory be to Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things, and to whom all return.)

These Tījān names possess many properties. Reciting them — provided your body, clothing, and surroundings are clean — or writing them and carrying them on your person, is very effective for attracting good or repelling evil. Were these names recited over mountains, the mountains would be torn apart. It is said that these names are the litany of Sayyid Meytatarun, master of the higher and lower spirits and of the spiritual kings. The scholars (ulema) have recorded that each name carries its own particular properties.

1st Name: Whoever writes the first name on a piece of paper, washes the writing off with water, and gives that water to his wife to drink, his wife will thereafter no longer do the things her husband dislikes.
2nd Name: Whoever writes the second name on a small piece of paper and, while casting the paper into flowing water, says:
.keza wa keza (O my Lord! I have written this petition to You so that You may grant my need, which is such-and-such.)
—whatever his wish may be, it will surely come to pass, by Allah's leave.

[I 487] 3rd Name: Whoever writes the third name on a piece of paper with saffron and rosewater, and an unmarried woman carries this writing on her person, that woman will marry in the shortest possible time.
4th Name: Whoever writes the fourth name on a piece of paper with saffron and rosewater and carries it on his person will be safe from fears, and, by Allah's leave, his debts will also be settled.
5th Name: Whoever writes the fifth name on a piece of paper and ties it to his right upper arm, then asks anyone for something, what he has asked for will be granted, by Allah's leave.
6th Name: Whoever writes the sixth name on a piece of paper with musk and saffron and carries it on his head will be safe from all evils.

7th Name: Whoever writes the seventh name on the palm of his hand, recites the name, states what he wishes to learn, and then lies down to sleep, a tribe of righteous jinn will come and show him in his dream the thing he wished to learn.

8th Name: Whoever, on account of a stolen or lost possession, first purifies himself and then writes the eighth name on his right leg and enters spiritual retreat (khalwa); if he recites the whole of the Tījān Invocation and asks Allah the Almighty for the return of his possession, seven spirits (rūḥānī) will come to him and tell him where his possession is.

9th Name: Whoever writes the ninth name on seven consecutive Fridays, washes the writing off with water each time, drinks most of the water, and wipes his face and chest with what remains, Allah the Almighty will enrich that person with great wealth. And whoever writes this ninth name and hangs it in his place of business, that place will become highly profitable.

10th Name: Whoever writes the tenth name on a piece of paper and hangs it on a weak person, that person will grow strong. If it is hung on a woman who is about to give birth, she will give birth easily. If it is hung on the right side of a person whose sexual power is weak, his sexual power will be strengthened.
11th Name: Whoever writes the eleventh name on his right palm and shakes hands with anyone, that person will come to love him greatly.
Whoever writes this name on a piece of paper and carries it between his eyes will defeat his enemies.

12th Name: Whoever writes this name, washes the writing off with water, drinks part of the water and washes his face with the rest, then appears before a judge — that judge will be struck with awe of him and will grant his request. O you who desire this science! Know the worth of this secret that has reached you, and honor what is due to it.
[I 488] The Exegesis of the Jeljelūtiyye and its Exalted Occult Properties (khawāṣṣ)

The science of spirit-lore (rūḥāniyya) is the very soul of the sciences of wisdom. This highly important and much-sought ʿazīma (a solemn spiritual working, here an invocation), known for its exalted worth, is the invocation called the Jeljelūtiyye. Because of the names it contains, the kasems (oaths) within it, the lofty secrets it holds, and its great properties, most of the sages and the masters of khawāṣṣ (occult properties) have spoken of this ʿazīma in the following terms.

The seeker (talib) must be upright both inwardly and outwardly. His livelihood must be lawful, and he must counsel his brothers in faith. He must keep away from what Allah the Exalted has forbidden in His noble Book and through the tongue of His generous Prophet. In every affair he must follow the noble Qur'an and the Sunnah, remain continually in a state of ritual purity, wear clean clothing, and perfume himself with pleasant scents. He must be wholly obedient to Allah, may He be glorified and exalted, and never associate partners with Him. He must perform his religious duties in the best manner and be sincere (Ikhlāṣ) toward Allah the Exalted in his acts of worship, for sincerity is the gate of union (vuslat). He must conceal the spiritual secrets he witnesses, and must never grow weary of asking, for whoever strives shall find his reward. He must take care to be moderate in his requests and must trust in fear of God (takva). He must be well versed in matters of religion, so that his proof (hujjet) stands firm and sharp before the spirits. In all his conduct, speech, and behaviour he must observe religious propriety.
Allah the Exalted has said thus in the noble Qur'an:
(Save those who repent, and correct themselves, and hold fast to Allah, and make their religion sincerely for Allah alone — these are with the believers.)
Allah the Exalted has likewise said on this matter:

[I 489] (Whoever hopes to meet his Lord, let him do righteous deeds and associate no one in the worship of his Lord.) For sincerity is the gate of union, while ostentation (riya) is the gate of estrangement and rejection.

The seeker must conceal the secrets he witnesses — the obedience of angels toward him, the appearance of the cinn (jinn) to him, his speaking with them, and his setting them to tasks. If he discloses these secrets to others, his standing among them diminishes. Even if the answer is delayed, he must not grow weary of asking, for weariness becomes the seeker's dead end and undoing. He must take care to be moderate in his requests, trust in fear of God, and know well the rulings of the Law, the invocations, and the declarations, so that he may hold firm proof and, by his knowledge, have authority over jinn who do not obey him. For whoever seeks this science stands in the rank of a ruler over men. He must observe Allah's Book and the authority of His Names. After writing something from the noble Qur'an or from the Names, he must not place it anywhere it might be trodden underfoot. He must face the qibla, sit in a clean place, and the place must contain no one in a state of ritual impurity (cenabet), no menstruating woman, no crying infant, no dog, and no image of an animal. He must guard and keep himself far from bad character, and from anything that violates uprightness and propriety.

Know also this: jinn and spirits are present everywhere. The jinn who dwell in a given place do not permit spirits who are muwakkil (assigned, governing) to Names and invocations outside their own to enter that place. This is only overcome when the seeker dismisses (sarf al-ummar) the resident inhabitants of that place. Therefore, before performing any amal (working) in a given place, the seeker must first drive out the jinn who dwell there. Once he has driven them out and completed his working, he must then command them to return to their places.

The finest and most sound form of sarf al-ummar that we have transmitted for dismissing jinn from a place is given below. To perform the sarf al-ummar, the seeker must burn kundur (frankincense), kizbere (coriander), shinuz, and fasuh as bakhūr (incense), and recite the following sarf al-ummar prayer three (3) times.
This is the sarf al-ummar prayer to be recited:
[I 492] Cellel muheymine munezzilil kurāni.
-I 493] After reciting this sarf al]
ummar prayer three (3) times, you begin your working, and once you have completed it, you say the following to send the jinn back :to their places

(By the truth of the names by which you were dismissed, O inhabitants of this place — He is the Living, the Sustainer. Neither slumber nor sleep overtakes Him. To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Who is there that can intercede with Him except by His permission? He knows what is before them and what is behind them, and they encompass nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursī (Throne/Footstool) extends over the heavens and the earth, and the preserving of them tires Him not. And He is the Most High, the Most Great.)

[I 494] When using the Celcelutiyye qasam, one must avoid error, avoid writing it incorrectly, must not read what comes later before what comes earlier or the reverse, and must under no circumstances make a mistake. For such errors spoil every qasam, and your working will come to nothing.

Know that the number of angels charged with this Celcelutiyye ʿazīma is eight. These eight angels are: Sayyid Rukyāīl, Sayyid Jebrāīl, Sayyid Semsemāīl, Sayyid Mīkāīl, Sayyid Sarfeyāīl, Sayyid Anyāīl, Sayyid Kesfeyāīl, and Sayyid Tahyatmaghyelyal. Tahyatmaghyelyal is their chief.

Each of these seven kings (melik) has a day of his own, on which he descends to the seeker. If the seeker's working is of great importance and consequence, the angel is invoked for it. The conditions for bringing them down are these: complete purity, wearing pleasant scents, facing the qibla, wearing white clothing, burning fragrant bakhūr, reciting the qasam with humble reverence (hushu), and, at the end, bowing the head in respect to the angel one wishes to bring down, praising Allah the Exalted both before and after the qasam. At the moment of the angel's descent, one must rise to one's feet, receive him with a smiling face and courteous manner, and pray. The prayer known from the earlier scholars, which may be recited for them, is as follows.
(May Allah strengthen you with the Greatest Light, and draw you nearer still to the noble, purified Presence for which He has made you worthy.)

The benefit of this prayer is that the angel will offer this very same prayer back on your behalf. When speaking with him, you should frame your questions with great care. If you have brought him down on account of a lowly khadim (attendant spirit), your form of address should be as follows.
(I ask you, O generous king, that you command so-and-so to do...)

[I 495] Know! The angels who are near to the presence of Allah the Exalted never slacken in their worship of Him. When the seeker addresses a question to an angel concerning something befitting his own station, his request must be brief and to the point, so that the angel may ascend again swiftly. The angel should be called upon for weighty matters — those things which the lowly hadims are unable to accomplish.

O seeker! Know well that the angels are of a different substance and clarity, and because the light of their radiance is so powerful, the eye of one who looks upon them cannot remain steady (mutemekkin) enough to behold them. Each angel has a distinguishing trait that sets him apart from the others.

Sayyid Rukyāīl: This angel descends into a dome of green silk. Atop the dome is a green banner. The dome's door stands open, and at Rukyāīl's side are five green-clad assistants in his service. When he descends to the seeker, he remains within the dome for a time before coming out to its doorway. A kursī (throne) of light is set up there for him. This angel descends on Sunday, and his khadim is Muzhib.

Sayyid Jebrāīl: This angel descends into a dome of light. Atop the dome is a yellow banner. He does not come out of the dome until the seeker addresses him with words. Jebrāīl has ten assistants, and he descends together with them. This angel descends on Monday, and his khadim is Ebyad.

Sayyid Semsemāīl: This angel descends into a dome of light. At the door of this dome are two red banners. Sayyid Semsemāīl has three assistants, and he descends together with them, standing at the dome's door. Sayyid Semsemāīl descends on Tuesday, and his khadim is Ahmer.

Sayyid Mīkāīl: This angel descends into a dome of light. On the right side of the dome is a white banner. Four assistants descend together with Mīkāīl and stand beneath the banner. Sayyid Mīkāīl descends on Wednesday, and his khadim is Burkān.

Sayyid Sarfeyāīl: This angel descends into a dome of light that is white and green. The dome has two doors. At each door stand ten assistants, and there are four renowned banners of white and green. On the left side of the dome stands a very tall angel named Salsayāīl, the chief of this company. Sayyid Sarfeyāīl descends on Thursday, and his khadim is Shemhūresh.
Sayyid Anyāīl: This angel descends into a dome of light together with six assistants and three banners. This angel descends on Friday, and his khadim is Zevbeah.
[I 496] Sayyid Kesfeyāīl: This angel descends into a dome of black light, together with thirty assistants and ten black banners. This angel descends on Saturday, and his khadim is Meymūn.

Talisman for the back of the mirror — a plain square frame with a word set at each corner; the centre reads "the name of the angel" [ism el-malak], marking where that name is to be written, between two rows of repeated letter hā. [I 496]

Sayyid Tahyatmaghliyāl: Before this angel descends, two domes descend first, each shining like a star with unmistakable brightness. Afterward a great dome descends between the two that came before it. Together with it come a thousand assistants; some of these stand around the dome, and others stand outside the rika (the gathering, or circle). It has fifty white banners. When Sayyid Tahyatmaghliyāl descends, the seven khuddām (servant-spirits) named earlier come and stand behind the rika. Not one of these seven khuddām may ever draw near to that rika.

To bring down Sayyid Tahyatmaghliyāl, in addition to the conditions mentioned earlier, the seeker's clothing must be entirely white, and the place where he sits must be clean and fragrant. It is a stipulated condition that none of these seven exalted angels may be dismissed until his obedience has been secured.

If the seeker's inner sight is veiled (mahcub), he must without fail have a skilled bakiji (seer) to look on his behalf. The seer must announce their arrival, so that the seeker can prepare to receive them. If he cannot find a skilled seer, he must find a boy or girl who has not yet reached puberty. On the forehead of the seer-child or the skilled seer, write the following names and verse:
and We removed from...) .
.(you your veil, so your sight, this Day, is sharp
After writing this, write the following talisman on the back of a mirror:

[I 497] and in its centre write the name of the angel, the assistant, or the khadim that is desired. Then hand the mirror to the seer and tell them to hold it and look into it. The seer-child must be able to see whomever you have brought down or summoned. Through the mirror, keshf (unveiled sight) is opened to the seer, who then understands what is being indicated.

If the seeker intends to bring these down and prepare the working himself, and his sight is not veiled, he may do so by means of a mirror. When he calls forth any one of these seven angels, he must observe and respect the rank of each of the seven. He must not belittle them with unseemly words, joke with them, or use coarse language. In their presence he must treat each one exactly as is fitting for him. What you ask of them must be a matter of true necessity — do not put them to the test merely to try them. Address kings gently, but address assistants firmly and sternly. Address avarit (jinn that afflict human beings), ummar, and karain (indwelling companion-spirits) with force, rebuke (zajr), and stern threat. If the seeker observes these things, he will command awe and his word will carry weight before them.

At the end of this act of bringing them down — whether it be the seven khuddām, the kings of the tribes, or the assistants under their command — you say, "Bārakallāhu fīkum wa ʿalaykum" (May Allah bless you and send His blessing down upon you). You say these same words also when sending them away.

The seeker should also know this well: certain amels have talismans (tilsam) particular to them. Those who understand this science deeply and possess true mastery of it have no need of these. But they make use of them anyway, to safeguard their knowledge and protect themselves from the eyes of the envious. If the seeker undertaking this work understands nothing of talismans, he must not proceed without first obtaining guidance from a trustworthy Sheyh (master), and he should place his trust in that Sheyh.

There are two methods of using the Celcelutiyye ʿazīma. The first method is for beginners: they make this ʿazīma into a regular wird (recurring devotional recitation) and draw on its properties. The benefit of adopting this ʿazīma as a wird is that it brings one close to the spirits, subdues (taskhir) them to oneself, and makes the response come more swiftly than by other means.

The first method for the Celcelutiyye qasam is this: one adopts this qasam as a wird and recites it once in the morning and once in the evening. Afterward, a ḥāja (matter of need) is presented to the reciter, and if the reciter wishes to fulfil it, he recites the Celcelutiyye qasam 1, 7, 21, or 41 times, whereupon the wish of the one who presented the ḥāja is granted.

[I 498] The second method for the Celcelutiyye qasam is this: a master of this science, without having adopted the ʿazīma as a wird, may simply recite it 41 times at the time of any need, and he will attain his wish by Allah the Exalted's leave. The number forty-one (41) is the highest and most perfect rank among numbers.

The following conditions are required for using the Tawkil (charge, or commissioning formula) given below: while reciting, keep your wish in mind, and especially while reading the seventeenth repetition, you must recite while thinking of your wish. During the recitation you must also burn that day's bakhūr. The buhurs for each day are as follows:

Sunday's bakhūr is Cavi (benzoin), Monday's bakhūr is Kafur (camphor), Tuesday's bakhūr is Kundur (frankincense), Wednesday's bakhūr is Meyatu saile, Thursday's bakhūr is Mastaki (mastic), Friday's bakhūr is Ud (agarwood) and Ned, Saturday's bakhūr is Udu hindi (Indian agarwood).
This is the Tawkil to be recited at the end of every recitation of the Celcelutiyye ʿazīma:

...(let it be thus, one and unlike any other. I ask you to send blessing and peace upon our master Muḥammad, and upon his family and companions, and that you do such-and-such and such-and-such. And may Allah send blessing upon our master Muḥammad and upon his family and companions, and grant them peace.)
These are the two methods that work through recitation alone. Without any writing, these two methods are excellent, and are well suited to those who cannot write and whose keshf is not open.
The Celcelutiyye ʿazīma has two khawatim (seals) — one of seven and one of eight.

The sevenfold seal [yedili khātam] — a 7×7 grid of the seven cryptic letter-signs (the seven letters absent from the Fātiḥa), each row shifted one place from the row above; no lettering outside the grid. [I 499]

The sages have long disputed the meaning of these forms made up of seven letters and have dwelt upon them at great length. But the truth is this: they must not be disclosed unless they are unveiled to the seeker by Allah the Exalted, whether through inspiration or in a dream. For these are among the hidden secrets.
There are seven letters that do not occur within the Noble Fātiḥa.
The symbolic meanings of these letters are as follows:
The letter Fe (8). Elhātem (the Seal).
The letter Jīm ((). Esselāse usiyyin (the three staffs).
The letter Shin (<). Elmīmit tamīsi (the truncated Mīm).
The letter Se (:). Sullem (the ladder).
[I 500] The letter Ẓāʾ (>). El-erbea enāmil (the four fingers).
The letter Khāʾ (9). El-hā'ish-shakīk (the twin Hā).
The letter Ze (+). Elwāwul mukawwes (the bent Wāw).
Each of these seven letters has a name of its own; these names are as follows:
The letter Fe (8) is the name Fard (the Single One) of Allah the Exalted.
The letter Jīm is the name Jebbār (the Compeller) of Allah the Exalted.
The letter Shin (<) is the name Shekūr (the Ever-Thankful) of Allah the Exalted.
The letter Se (:) is the name Sābit (the Constant) of Allah the Exalted.
The letter Ẓāʾ (>) is the name Zāhir (the Manifest) of Allah the Exalted.
The letter Khāʾ (9) is the name Habīr (the All-Aware) of Allah the Exalted.
The letter Ze (+) is the name Zekī (the Pure) of Allah the Exalted.

If the Celcelutiyye ʿazīma (incantation) is to be used for reciting and writing, this is its most perfect form. For any wish, after writing the khātam, you write the Celcelutiyye ʿazīma and its tawkil (the formula that commissions the governing spirit) around the khātam. There is no particular day appointed for the reciting or writing of this ʿazīma. After writing the khātam, you hang it upon a rod. The best rod is a pomegranate rod. This rod must also have three branches. Burning the bakhūr (incense) proper to the day, you recite the ʿazīma together with the tawkil, just as we have described before. When you have finished reciting, take the writing down from the rod; if the object you seek is a good one, carry the writing upon you. If it is an ill one, place the writing in a suitable spot.

Let us render the Syriac names that occur within the Celcelutiyye ʿazīma into the Arabic tongue and present them to seekers, so that it may be of full benefit. And after me, offer up a righteous prayer.

Know this: Allah the Exalted has concealed many secrets within this exalted Celcelutiyye ʿazīma. It possesses such great properties that they cannot be contained in books, and no one can ever reach their end.
With this glorious ʿazīma the seeker gains mastery over everything he desires. He can draw benefit to himself, repel evil, and do all manner of similar things.

[I 522] The Glorious Khawāṣṣ (occult Properties) of the Tahātīli Sabaa These seven Syriac names are called the Tahātīli Seba. These names possess hidden secrets and properties. The Tahātīli Seba belongs among the concealed mysteries. The Tahātīli Seba holds a very great secret, one that no one has the power to unravel. As long as you make use of these names, you will have no need of any other knowledge.

If you are content with what Allah the Exalted has decreed for you, you will attain your purpose in whatever you wish, whether it be for good or for ill. May Allah the Exalted grant you benefit and blessing through this. Only the masters of this science know its worth. You!
Understand its secret well.

If a single letter is taken from the start of each name and recited together with the eighth name, Limukfencil, which serves as their zimam (binding name), the one who recites it can halt armies and ships.
He defeats the armies of tyrants, and routs oppressors and despots. He stands fearless before kings. These blessed names also have a very great effect in the burning of jinn and devils.

You perform this working on the last Wednesday of the Arabic month, while the Moon is in the sign of Gemini, and cast the names upon the talismanned place. This nullifies every obstacle and talisman of that place, and every harmful nāmus (baleful occult force), whirlwind, arrow, wind, missile, sandstorm, earthquake, bolt of lightning, sword, crocodile, beast, and the like. At the same time it cancels obstacles such as jinn, devils, celestial and terrestrial ifrits, apparitions, sleep-paralysis, sleep, palsy, fear, plague, mercury poisoning, harmful blades, howling creatures, scorpions, fire, and smoke. For these belong to the hidden Book of the Manifest. It is the essence of knowledge and the key to treasures.
The names of the Tahātīli Seba are these:
Liltahtil Mehtahtil Kahtaytil Fehtaytil Nehhattil Jehhattil Lahhattil.
The eighth name, formed from the initial letters of these names and serving as their zimam, is:
Limukfencil.

[I 523] 1. If you wish to see spiritual beings and speak with them: Perform a complete ritual ablution, and enter a seventy (70) day retreat in a clean place. After performing a two-rak'ah prayer of need, recite the Tahatili Seba (a sevenfold invocatory formula) seventy (70) times after every obligatory prayer, and complete the seventy days in this way. On the seventy-first day, write the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa (the seven names) on the heart of a vulture, then burn the heart thoroughly, pound it well, and work it into a paste like kohl. Apply what you have prepared to your eyes as kohl, drawing it on with a gold probe. You will then see the spiritual beings around you clearly. Whatever you wish to ask of them, they will carry out swiftly, and they will also inform you of news concerning the world.

2. If you wish to break a talisman guarding buried treasure, or to nullify talismanic water and other obstructions: on eight items — stone, a potsherd, leather, meerschaum, a piece of a bowl, gold, silver, copper, lead, tin, paper, or anything similar — write the Tahatili Seba in ḥurūfu muqaṭṭaʿ (letters written in their separate, unjoined forms), one name on each piece. After writing them, begin walking through the talismanic site. Walk a little into the place and cast down the first name in front of you. Walk a little further and cast down the second name. Continue walking slowly like this, and cast down the sixth name at the spot where the talismanic water is. But keep the seventh and eighth names in your left hand, and do not let go of them if you can help it — if you release them, the khuddām (servant spirits) will do you harm. In this way the obstructions or the talismanic water at that place will be nullified. Once the work is finished, if it is possible to retrieve the names from where you cast them, keep the seventh and eighth names in your left hand and gather up the cast names with your right hand. If it is not possible to retrieve the names you cast, leave them where they are. Keep those two names safe in your hand. The muwakkilun (governing spirits) will return to their places and posts. Should the companions with you wish to harm you or kill you, take the eighth name from your left hand into your right hand and say:
Ya huddame hazihil asmāʾ ihtefuzuni an uyuni bi hakkiha ʿalaykum.
(O servants of this name, by its truth, conceal me from the eyes of my companions.)
In this way you will be hidden from your companions' eyes, and protected by Allah's leave.

[I 524] 3. If you wish to nullify talismanic water: write the Tahatili Seba separately on stone, on a leaf, or on paper. After writing them, go to the place where the talismanic water is, and place the first, second, third, and fourth names at the four corners of the site. If you then cast the remaining three names into the talismanic water, the water will vanish.
Once the work is finished, remove the three names you cast into the water; otherwise the water will gush back up and return.

If something harmful appears at that place, make a figure out of wax, place a sword or spear in the figure's hand, and inscribe the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa upon the figure. Present the figure at that spot, and the talisman will be nullified by Allah's leave.

4. Take seven small stones, and after reciting the Tahatili Seba once over each stone, cast them to your right, your left, behind you, and in front of you; you will then be hidden from the eyes of your enemies by Allah's leave.

5. If you wish to put out fire and smoke at a talismanic place: take a portion of fire, cast a fragrant bakhūr (incense) upon it, and recite the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa. Then write the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa on a plate, wash the writing off with water, and, walking slowly, sprinkle that water over the place. The fire and smoke at that place will be put out.

6. If hideous, savage forms (such as a snake, a scorpion, a lion, a mule, or other predatory animals) appear before you at a talismanic place, make the shape of that animal out of wax. Inscribe the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa on the figure you have made, and fume it with incense. If you then cast that figure into the talismanic place, the talisman will be rendered void by Allah's leave.

7. If the door shuts on you when you enter a talismanic place, write the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa on the door, and the talisman will be nullified and the door will open. Or else, place the first name beneath the threshold, the second, third, fourth, and fifth names at the four corners of the place, and the sixth name in the middle of the place. If you also hold the seventh name in your left hand, then, by Allah's leave, every obstruction, talisman, and moving thing will be nullified.

8. To nullify talismanic water: write the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa separately on any material (leather, paper, lead, or the like). After arriving at the talismanic place, walk slowly and cast the first and second names to your right, the third name to your left, the fourth name behind you, the fifth name in front of you, the sixth name in the middle of the place, the seventh name beside the door of the place, and the eighth name into the talismanic water — for [I 525] the eighth name is for nullifying the water. But together with the eighth name you also write these noble verses:

A chain of noble verses on drought) and vanishing water — among them "or its water sinks away, so that you will never be able to seek it out," and "they ask you about the mountains: say, my Lord will scatter them into dust, leaving the land a bare, level plain" — joined here with words recalling how the sea parted for Musa son of Imran and the Jordan for Isa son of Maryam, peace be upon him, and closing with the warning: "We (".shall draw them on by degrees from where they do not know
In this way the water will stop and the talisman will be nullified. Or else, together with the eighth name, you write this noble verse:
Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm. Kul eraeytum in esbeha maukum ghawran femen ye'tikum bimain muin.
(Say: "Have you considered — if your water were to sink into the ground, who then could bring you flowing water?")
[I 526] on a bowl and cast it into the water, the water's helper will be destroyed and the water will stop.
To divide, set at enmity, and ruin the household of oppressors who have banded together to harm others
While Qamar is in a fire sign, write the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa, the name of the maṭlūb (the object of the working), and the letters of the fire element on a potsherd

While Qamar is in an air sign, write the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa on a piece of paper together with the name of the maṭlūb's mother and the letters of the air element, fume it with a sweet-smelling incense, and hang it facing into the wind
While Qamar is in a water sign, write the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa on a piece of paper together with the name of the maṭlūb's mother and the letters of the water element
If you wish to stir up violent love and bring your maṭlūb to you
If you wish to empty one dovecote and have the pigeons come and settle in another

15. If you wish to stop a turning mill, a turning water-wheel, or anything else that turns: while Qamar is in an earth sign that is also a turning (cardinal) sign, write the seventh name, and if you place it on the turning mill, the turning water-wheel, or whatever turning thing you wish to stop, it will stop at once.

16. If you wish to stop a mount: write the Asmāʾ al-Sitte (the six names) on a piece of paper and place it on the mount you wish to stop, in a way that cannot be seen. Then write the seventh name on another piece of paper and carry it on yourself. That mount will not be able to leave without taking you with it; even if it has already left, it will return in the shortest possible time.
If you wish to bind a man who has committed adultery to the woman with whom he committed it

18. If labour is violent and difficult, and you wish to ease the birth: write the eighth name and give its water to the woman struggling in labour to drink; she will give birth at once, by Allah's leave.

19. For a woman who miscarries: write the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa on seven separate pieces of paper with musk and saffron (one name on each paper). Each morning let her drink one name's water on an empty stomach. Begin with the first name on the first day, a Sunday, and continue for seven days. Then, on the eighth day, also a Sunday, write the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa again and let the woman [I 528] wash herself with its water. If the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa is written once more and the woman carries these names on her person, she will not miscarry again, by Allah's leave.

20. If you should be forced to go before someone whose malice you fear, write the eighth name with musk and saffron on a white piece of paper and place it under your cap. Then write the remaining six names on your right palm; when you go before the person you fear, you will be safe from his malice — indeed, that person will show you great respect.
21. If you wish to relieve a female mule's stomach ache: write the eighth name on the hooves of her four feet, and, by Allah's leave, the stomach ache will pass and she will recover.
If you wish to make someone accept you, stir them up, and bind their tongue against you

23. For a person afflicted by the evil eye (naẓar): recite the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa over water and give the water to the afflicted person to drink. Then take a linen cord seven spans long, recite the Asmāʾ al-Sabaa once over the cord, and pass the cord once around the person. Repeat this same act six times. After reciting and circling seven times in all, measure from the person's right shoulder to his right hand, and likewise from his left shoulder to his left hand. If the cord measures the same on both sides, the person has not been afflicted by the evil eye. If the cord is longer, whoever cast the eye is someone who loves him. If the cord is shorter, the eye that struck him belongs to someone malevolent who does not love him. Continue this procedure until the cord comes out even. But while you circle the cord around the person, never once let it touch the ground! When you have finished the working, roll up the cord and hang it upon the afflicted person; he will be healed by Allah's leave.

24. To remove large boils: if you write the eighth name around the boil, the boils will disappear by Allah's leave. If there is swelling on the body, write the eighth name on a plate, wash off the writing with oil, and if this oil is rubbed on the boils, healing will come by Allah's leave.
25. For stomach ache, write the eighth name on your palm and lick the writing off on an empty stomach; the stomach ache will pass by Allah's leave.

26. Write the seventh name on a white piece of paper on a Saturday at sunrise. After writing it, wax the paper, place it under your tongue, [I 529] and go before whichever judge, prominent and influential person, or person you fear; that person's tongue will be bound against you by Allah's leave, and he will speak well of you.

27. If you wish to release someone who has been bound, or to nullify the sorcery worked upon someone bewitched: write the first and eighth names on seven pieces of paper. After writing, standing over the bound person and saying:
Ya huddame hazel ism hallu zekere fulān ibni fulaneh an ferci fulāna binti fulaneh.
(O servants of this name, release the member of so-and-so son of so-and-so toward the private parts of so-and-so daughter of so-and-so.)
burn the papers one after another, and the person's binding will be released.
Or, in the case of someone bewitched, saying:
Ya huddame hazel ism hallul eshari an fulān ev fulāna.
(O servants of this name, undo the sorcery from so-and-so, man or woman.)
burn the papers one after another, and that person's sorcery will be nullified.

28. If you wish to protect a person or an animal from the evil eye: take a piece of cotton cord and measure it against the body of that person or animal. After measuring, recite the seventh name seven times and say:
Ya huddame hazel ism israfu ma bi hazihil jusseti min al- ayn.
(O servants of this name, dispel from this body whatever comes from the evil eye.)
The person or animal will then be safe from the evil eye by Allah's leave.

[I 587] The Qasam of Halhalat al-hawāʾ Wa Fatḥal-jawāʾ The great scholar Ahmed bin Ali el-Būnī (r.a.) — a man whose learning was as vast as the sea, and the unrivalled Imam of his age — has related the following concerning Halhalat al-hawāʾ wa Fatḥal-jawāʾ ["the Anklet-Rings of the Air and the Loosening of the Response"] and the contemplation of the higher spirits.

The Byzantine Emperor (Kayser) sent a letter to Hazreti Omer (r.a.), in which he wrote: "O Ebū Hafs! We have found in the Psalms, the Torah, and the Gospel that whoever recites a certain sura, Allah the Exalted forbids the Fire to touch that person's bones, for within it are seven letters. Have you yourselves found this in the book you call the Noble Qur'an — the book revealed to you, which you claim to be the most excellent of all books?" Hazreti Omer (r.a.) read the letter, showed it to Hazreti Ali (k.r.v.), and said: "O Ali! The Byzantine Emperor has sent us a letter. In it he says there is a sura containing seven letters, and that reciting it makes Allah (c.c.) forbid the Fire to touch one's bones." Hazreti Ali (k.r.v.) said, "Give me the letter." Having read it, he said: "O Omer, this sura is the Fātiḥa. The Prophet (s.a.v.) himself said so. These seven letters were once taken out of the Fātiḥa and placed into the Sūra Yā-Sīn; later they were taken from Yā-Sīn and placed into the Sūra el-En'ām. That verse is this:" Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm. Eve men kane meyten feahyeynahu wa cealna lahu nuran yemshi bihi finnasi kemen meseluhu fiz zulumati leyse biharicin minha kezalike zuyyine.

(In the name of Allah, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Is he who was dead, and to whom We gave life and set for him a light by which he walks among men, like him who is in darkness, unable to leave it? Thus it has been made to seem fair...)
The seven letters contained within this verse are these:

Ze Khāʾ Ẓāʾ Se Shīn Jīm Fe Hazreti Omer (r.a.) said: "O Ali, let us send word to the Byzantine Emperor." The two of them then prostrated together before Allah (c.c.), the Almighty and Glorious, and [I 588] afterward sent their reply to the Emperor by letter. When the Emperor received it, his heart found peace; he came to believe, and he died in the faith of Islam.
The name formed by combining these seven letters is one to which the Most Exalted Name of Allah is answerable. It is the name (Fejeshin Sezhazin).

The servants of this name are the spirits (rūḥānī) that serve as muwakkil (governing spirits) over the seven planets. At the same time, this name holds sway over the kings who rule the earth. Each of these letters has its own angel, planet, zodiac sign, day, month, and name.

The letter Ẓāʾ: Its planet is Jupiter, its zodiac sign is Sagittarius, its celestial angel is (Sarfeyāīl), peace be upon him, its terrestrial angel is (Shemhuresh), its day is Thursday, and its month is November.
