The ink of the planet Moon is beyādil zijāj (white clove).
The Taṣrīf (operative Procedure) of Halhalat al-hawāʾ Wa Fatḥal-jawāʾ
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 589
If you wish to possess the taṣrīf of Halhalat al-hawāʾ, make a suret (effigy) out of paper. Once you have made it, write the following on the effigy's head:
Ahmar Semsemail Akreb Mirrīkh Shin On the effigy's face, write the following:
Ebyad Anyail Sevr Zuhra Khāʾ On the effigy's neck and arms, write the following:
Murreh Jibrīl Seratan Qamar Jīm [I 590] On the effigy's chest, write the following:
Muzhib Rukyail Esed Shams Fe On the effigy's back, write the following:
Shemhuresh Sarfeyail Kavs Mushtarī Ẓāʾ On the effigy's belly, write the following:
Burkan Mīkāʾīl ʿUṭārid Cevza Se On the effigy's two legs and two knees, write the following:
Meymun Kesfeyail Deliv Zuḥal Ze You must write upon the effigy in this exact order, for this is the true arrangement.

If, using this Halhalat al-hawāʾ Qasam, you wish to burn the jinn possessing a body, or to torment it: seat the afflicted patient before you and write the khātam on the patient's hand. Recite the Qasam over him until he falls into a seizure. Once the patient seizes, say "Confine it!" — and they will confine the jinn afflicting him. Whatever you then command, they will do. If you tear off a piece of the effigy you made earlier, the corresponding limb of the afflicting jinn will be torn off as well.

If you wish to burn the jinn afflicting the patient: throw the effigy you made into the fire. The afflicting jinn will have no escape and will burn. But before doing this, make the jinn speak, and ask it why it came, when it entered the patient's body, its name, its tribe, its planet, and its dwelling place.

If you wish to confine the jinn afflicting the patient in a glass bottle: write the khātam on a piece of silk cloth, and draw seven circles upon the khātam. If the amal (the working) falls on a Sunday, write the khātam on yellow silk; on Monday, on white silk; on Tuesday, on red silk; on Wednesday, on blue silk; on Thursday, on green silk; on Friday, on grey silk; [I 591] and on Saturday, write the khātam on black silk. After writing the khātam on the silk, place the glass bottle in the center of the silk bearing the khātam, and recite the Qasam until the jinn enters the bottle. If the jinn says, "I am of the same kind as this cloth," it has spoken truly; if it says, "I am not of the cloth's kind," it has lied. Then write that day's letter upon the silk, set the cloth alight, and make the patient breathe in its smoke through the nose until the jinn enters the bottle. Once the jinn has entered, seal the bottle's mouth with wax, and on the wax write these letters: Ze, Khāʾ, Ẓāʾ, Se, Shīn, Jīm, Fe. Then bury the bottle in an empty place. Until that bottle is broken, the jinn cannot escape from within it.

If you wish to beat the jinn before confining it: write the khātam on a piece of leather. After writing it, command the jinn to enter into the khātam. Beforehand, write these letters on a rod: Ze, Khāʾ, Ẓāʾ, Se, Shīn, Jīm, Fe. Strike the leather bearing the khātam with this inscribed rod. The moment you strike it, you will hear the jinn cry out. Then forgive the jinn, and ask it its name, its tribe, why it took possession, why it did what it did, its reasons, and whatever else you wish to know — you will receive its answer.
If you wish to send that jinn into a person of your choosing, you say the following
If you wish for the helāk (destruction/ruin) of an enemy or an oppressor
The Great Taṣarruf (dominion/working) of Halhalat al-hawāʾ Wa Fatḥal-jawāʾ
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 592

If you wish to gain possession of the taṣrīf and the spirits (rūḥāniyya) of this Qasam called Halhalat al-hawāʾ, which contains within it the prayer of the Ism al-Aʿẓam [the Greatest Name of Allah]: avoid all that is harām (forbidden), and after purifying yourself both inwardly and outwardly, for the sake of Allah's good pleasure, [I 593] fast for seven (7) days. Then fast for a further seven (7) days while observing riyāzat (ascetic discipline). On the fifteenth (15th) day, still fasting, enter a seven-day khalwa (spiritual retreat) beginning on a Sunday. Wear differently colored garments each day, and use bakhūr.

On Sunday, wear yellow garments; on Monday, white garments; on Tuesday, red garments; on Wednesday, blue garments; on Thursday, green garments; on Friday, grey garments; and on Saturday, black garments.

Your ink, too, must match the days and garments in the same way. Write each letter of the khātam with its own proper ink. Each day at sunrise, stand upon the tips of your big toes and recite Sūra Ṭā-Hā, Sūra Yā-Sīn, and Sūra Tebāreke. After reciting them, offer the ṣalawāt (blessings) upon our Prophet Hazreti Muḥammad (s.a.v.) seventy (70) times, in this form:
Allāhumma salli ala sayyidinā Muhammedin wa ala jemii eshabi Muḥammad.
(O Allah, send blessings upon our master Muḥammad and upon all the Companions of Muḥammad.)

After this, recite the Qasam once, from beginning to end, and speak that day's spirit-name (rūḥānī ism). On the first night of the third week (the week of the khalwa), a hādim (attendant spirit) full of light, dignified and reverent, will come to you. This hādim will speak with you. Take a shart (pledge) from it that it will serve you.

On Monday night, two persons will come to you and speak with you in the most beautiful words. They too are dignified and radiant of face. Take a pledge from these two as well, that they will serve you.
On Tuesday night, three persons will come to you. When you see them, stand firm and do not be afraid! Allah the Exalted says in the Noble Qur'an:
Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm. Yusebbitullahul lezine amenu bil kavlis sabiti fil hayatid dunya.
(Allah keeps those who believe firm upon a steadfast word, both in this world and in the Hereafter.)
Take a pledge from them as well. Never send any of them to do anything that is not pleasing to Allah the Exalted.
[I 594] On Wednesday night, four persons will come to you. They have a radiance like the moon, and their hair is sable-dark, hanging loose behind them. Take a pledge from them as well.

On Thursday night, five persons will come to you. They wear crowns on their heads and embroidered silk upon their bodies, and their faces are as radiant as those of the prophets. Guard against fitne (temptation/discord) and stand firm. Remain occupied with your working, and take a pledge from them as well. Allow no other thought into your mind — occupy yourself with nothing but your working.

On Friday night, six persons will come to you. They appear as if they were Persians. Each of them holds a rod in hand, their waists are girded tightly with belts, and they wear crowns on their heads; their hair, too, is filled with light. If you stand firm, you will attain what the men of ahwāl (states), akwāl (sayings), efāl (deeds), and ehwāl (fearsome states) have attained.

On Saturday night, seven persons will come to you. They too are like Persians (Iranian, non-Arab). These persons are the khuddām (spirit-servants) of the Halhalat al-hawāʾ Qasam. Take a pledge from them as well, for their service.

When you enter into these invocations and prayers, you must free yourself of distracting thoughts (family, wealth, joy, sorrow, fear, and the like). You must even keep yourself free of vesvese (whispered doubts). Occupy yourself with nothing but your working! Every letter in the khātam of taṣarruf has an angel that serves it. Understand this very well.
7×7 letter wafq — forty-nine cells of Arabic letters, each row a one-step cyclic shift of the row above; no labelling. [I 594]
7×7 letter wafq built on the seven letters absent from Sūrat al-Fātiḥa, each row repeating the sequence shifted one place; no headings or labels appear in the figure. [I 594]
The khawatim of the days are as follows:
The khātam of Sunday: The khātam of Monday:
Companion 7×7 letter wafq on the same seven letters, the cycle begun one letter further along; rows are successive one-step shifts; no headings or labels. [I 595]
Third 7×7 letter wafq in the same series, starting the seven-letter cycle at the next letter; rows are successive one-step shifts; no headings or labels. [I 595]
[I 595] The khātam of Tuesday: The khātam of Wednesday:
Fourth 7×7 letter wafq in the same series, the seven-letter cycle again advanced by one starting letter; no headings or labels. [I 595]
Fifth 7×7 letter wafq in the same series, the seven-letter cycle advanced by one further starting letter; no headings or labels. [I 595]
The khātam of Thursday: The khātam of Friday:
Two further 7×7 letter awfāq side by side: the left with cells left blank along a diagonal band, the right with an added bottom row of seven talismanic cipher signs; no labels. [I 596]
[I 596] This is the seal (khātam) for the day of Saturday — also called the Seal of Use.
This is the Qasam (the Oath, a set invocatory formula) of Halhalat al-hawāʾ wa Fetkul Ceva:

[I 602] sallallahu ala sayyidinā muhammedin wa ala alihi wa sahbihi wa sellim. Bismillahil [I 603] mutedani fi ulivvihil muteali fi denevvihil muteceberru bi ceberutihil munferidi bil izzeti wa-l- kibriya-i fela ilahe illallahul ferdul kaimu ves sultanid daimullezi hadaat lehul muluki wa sara kullil meliki li azameti memluki fatiris semavati wa-l- arḍi cailil mela-iketi rasulen uli ecnihatin mensa wa selase wa ruba-a yezidu fil halki ma yesha-u innallahe ala kulli shayʾin kadir.

(This opens with blessings upon the Prophet Muḥammad, then a doxology extolling God's transcendence and unmatched majesty, echoing the Qur'anic verse on the angels as messengers with wings — two, three, and four — and closing with: "God has power over all things.")

Aksemtu ʿalaykum eyyetuhel ervahir ruhaniyyetit tahiretiz zekiyyeti min al- envaril cevheriyyetil ghaniyyeti min al- eshhasil cevheriyyetis seniyyeti min al- envaris satiatil musherrefatil bekiyyeti aksemtu ʿalaykum bil ismis seri-ir refi-il muni-il mahcubil matlubil mahzunil meknun wa huwa ismullahil azimul a'zamu ism zatis sebati ahrifu evemen kane meyten feahyeynahu wa cealna lahu nuran yemshi bihi finnasi kemen meseluhu fiz zulumati leyse bi haricin minha kezalike zuyyine Allahu la ilahe illa huwel hayyul kayyumu wa ilahukum ilahun wahidun la ilahe illahuwer rahmanir rahimu munevveri fejeshin sezhazin shejezin Allahu Ferdun Cebbarun Shekurun Sabitun Zahirun Habirun Zekiyyun Allahumme Ferdun Cebbarun Ya Shekurun Ya Sabitun Ya Zahirun Ya Habirun Ya Zekiyyun Ya Allahu ilahuna wa ilahun kulli shayʾin ilahun vahidun la ilahe illa anta Ya Zelcelali wa-l-ikram.

(I adjure you, O pure and radiant spiritual souls, luminous and jewel-like, hidden and cherished, by the swift, exalted, response-granting Name, the sought-after and treasured, the hidden and preserved — which is the Greatest Name of God, the Name of the Everlasting Essence; the letters of "was he not dead, and We gave him life, and set for him a light by which to walk among men — like one who is in darkness and cannot leave it." Thus it is made fair: God, there is no god but He, the Living, the Self-Subsisting; your god is One God, there is no god but He, the Merciful, the Compassionate — followed by a string of divine Names: the One, the Compeller, the Ever-Thankful, the Firm, the Manifest, the All-Aware, the Pure — invoked again as vocatives, closing with "O Lord of Majesty and Bounty.")

Allāhumma inni tewesseltu ileyke bi ḥaqqi ismikel azimul a'zamu en tesharali ruhaniyeti hazel ism yahdumini wa yerau ḥaqqi feinni lillahi ala ahdihi wa misakihi wa la asrufi ehaden minkum fi ma'siyyetihi wa kane ahdi rabbi mesulen feinneke entellahu ala ma tesha-u kadir. Ecib Ya Rukyail wa anta Ya Jibrīl wa anta Ya Semsemail wa anta Ya Mīkāʾīl wa anta Ya Sarfeyail wa anta Ya Anyail wa anta Ya Kesfeyail wa bi ḥaqqi men leyse kemislihi sheyun fil arḍi wa la fis sema-i wa huwes semi-ul basir. Wa bihakki men bi yedihi melekuti kulli shayʾin wa huwa yujiru wa la yujaru ʿalayhi. Wa bi ḥaqqi men emruhu beynel kafi ven nun. Innema emruhu iza erade sheyen en yekulehu kun feyekun. Wa bi ḥaqqi men yuhyil izame wa hiye ramim. Illa ma emertum kulli vahidun minkum hadimen min al- jinni in shi'te ev min al- mela-iketi en eradtihum yahdimuni wa yera-i ḥaqqi wa yefalu ma uridu wa asrifuhu fi jemi-i havaic min emrid dini ved dunya wa lillahi ala ahdihi wa misakihi la asrifu ahaden minkum fi ma'siyyetihi wa kane ahdi rabbi mesulen.

(O God, I entreat You by the truth of Your Greatest Name, that You make the spiritual essence of this Name serve me and respect my due, for I stand by God's covenant and pledge and will not employ any of you in disobedience to Him — my Lord's covenant shall be held to account, for You, God, have power over all that You will. Answer, O Rukyail — and you, O Jibrīl — and you, O Semsemail — and you, O Mīkāʾīl — and you, O Sarfeyail — and you, O Anyail — and you, O Kesfeyail — by the truth of Him who has no likeness on earth or in the heavens, He who is the Hearing, the Seeing; by the truth of Him in whose hand is the dominion of all things, who protects and cannot be resisted; by the truth of Him whose command is between the Qāf and the Nun, for His command, when He wills a thing, is only to say to it "Be," and it is; by the truth of Him who gives life to bones after they have decayed. Each of you must give me a servant — of the jinn if you wish, or of the angels, as you see fit — to serve me and respect my due, to do as I ask, and I shall employ him in all my needs, of religion and of the world; and I stand by God's covenant and pledge, and will not employ any of you in disobedience to Him — my Lord's covenant shall be held to account.)

Allāhumma inni eseluke bismikel azimullezi aleyte bihi fetecelleyte bihi li musa bin Imran fevka cebele turi sina wa bit [I 604] turi wa-l- kitabil mesturi wa b ima ensade-a min re'sil cibali wa eseluke Allāhumma bi kerameti hazihil isharetilleti tekaddemet bi kelimetihi ta'zimike esmaike ya huwa bel huwehu fi izzi izzihi la yehuli va la yezuli wa la yuhitu bihil efhami wa la illa wa hamin wa lel ukuli aksemtu ʿalaykum bihi Ya Rukyail wa anta Ya Jibrīl wa anta Ya Semsemail wa anta Ya Mīkāʾīl wa anta Ya Sarfeyail wa anta Ya Anyail wa anta Ya Kesfeyail illa ma emertum hadimen min al- jinni yetemesselu emri wa yera-i ḥaqqi wa lillahi ala ahdihi wa misakihi en la asrifu ahaden minkum fi ma'siyyetillahi teala wa kane ahdi rabbi mesula.

(O God, I ask You by Your Mighty Name, by which You rose high and revealed Yourself to Musa son of Imran atop Mount Sinai, and by the Mount, and by the Written Book, and by what echoed forth from the mountaintops; and I ask You, O God, by the sanctity of this sign that has gone before, by the word of Your reverence for Your Names — O He, He alone, in the glory of His glory, who neither changes nor passes away, whom minds cannot encompass, nor understanding, nor intellects grasp. I adjure you by Him, O Rukyail, and you, O Jibrīl, and you, O Semsemail, and you, O Mīkāʾīl, and you, O Sarfeyail, and you, O Anyail, and you, O Kesfeyail: you must give me a servant of the jinn to embody my command and respect my due, and I stand by God's covenant and pledge not to employ any of you in disobedience to God Most High — my Lord's covenant shall be held to account.)

Allāhumma inni eseluke bil asmāʾ-il mektubeti fi suadiku arshike wa bil asmāʾ-il muhitatu bis semavatis sebi wa-l- ardines Sabaa wa hiye Ahiyyen sherahiyyen edunayi esbautin ali sheddayi tealeytu ilahi ulivven kebiren wa teazemtu min azimi wa tekaddes min rabbi majidu azimu bel huwa huwehu fi izzihi la yehuli wa la yezuli wa la yuhitu bihi min al-evhami wa-l- ukulu.

(O God, I ask You by the Names inscribed on the pillars of Your Throne, and by the Names encompassing the seven heavens and the seven earths — Ahiyyen, Sherahiyyen, Edunayi, Esbautin, Ali Sheddayi — You are exalted, O my God, in great loftiness, magnified beyond all magnitude, sanctified beyond my Lord's glory — He alone, in the glory of His glory, who neither changes nor passes away, whom fancies and intellects cannot encompass.)

ecibu ya meashirel ervahir ruhaniyyetibil ismillezi yedu bihil ervahil faniyyeti feyeiduha lilecsadil baliyyeti wesh sheurul muntesiratu ilel cemacimin nehireti elvahan elvahan elacele elacele essaate essaate Allahu aghlibu wa aghlibul batilu yezhaku wa yuzhebu wa-l- hakku ya'li wa yerhebu demeytikum bi shai lamii wa nura satia haysu ma zehebe minkum zahiben wa la yerciu minkum racia innema tuadune levakia istesartu ʿalaykum billahil ghafuru wa bitturi wa-l- makamil mesturi wa rakkin menshurin wa-l- beytil ma'muri wa bima ensadea min ra'sil cibali wa bi kerameti hazihil ishareti elvahan elvahan elacele elacele essaate essaate bi ḥaqqi Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm.

(Answer, O company of spiritual spirits, by the Name through which the perished souls are recalled, so that they are restored to the decayed bodies, and the hair scattered upon the bleached skulls is gathered again — hasten, hasten, quickly, quickly, this very hour, this very hour! God is Victorious, and falsehood is vanquished, brought low and swept away, while the truth is exalted and feared. I have threatened you with a flashing blade and a radiant fire, so that whoever among you departs shall not return — for indeed what you are promised shall surely come to pass. I have called upon you by God the All-Forgiving, and by the Mount, and by the Hidden Station, and by the Unrolled Scroll, and by the Frequented House, and by what echoed forth from the mountaintops, and by the sanctity of this sign: hasten, hasten, quickly, quickly, this very hour, this very hour — by the truth of "In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.")

Bismillahil muteali denevvihil mutedani ulivvihil muteceberru bi ceberutihil munferidi bil izzeti wa-l- kibriya-i fela ilahe illallahul ferdul kaimu ves sultanid daimillezi hadaat lehul muluki wa sara kullil meliki li azameti memluki fatiris semavati wa-l- arḍi cailil mela-iketi rasulen uli ecnihati mensa wa selase wa ruba-i yezidu fil halki ma yesha-u innallahe ala kulli shayʾin kadir. Aksemtu ʿalaykum eyyetuhel ervahir ruhaniyyetit tahiretiz zekiyyeti min al- envaril cevheriyyetis seniyyeti min al- eshhasil musherrefetis satiati behiyyeti aksemtu ʿalaykum bil ismis refi-ir rubani wa zatis sebati ahrifu evemen kane meyten feahyeynahu wa cealna lahu nuran yemshi bihi finnasi kemen meseluhu fiz zulumati leyse bi haricin minha kezalike zuyyine aksemtu aleykum ya meashirel ervahir [I 605] ruhaniyetit tahiratiz zekiyyeti min al- envaril cevheriyyetis seniyyeti min al- eshhasil musherrefetis satiatil heybeti aksemtu aleykum bi hakkil ismis seri-ir rafi-ir rubani wa huwa ismillahil azimul a'zamu fejeshin sezhazin Allahu Ferdun Cebbarun Shekurun Sabitun Zahirun Habirun Zekiyyun (This entire section repeats the opening adjuration in slightly varied form — again invoking God's transcendence, the winged angel-messengers, and the pure spiritual souls, by the swift, exalted, celestial Name.)

ecib billahi ʿalayka Ya Rukyail anta wa huddamike miner ruhaniyeti wa-l- ardiyyeti bi ḥaqqi ma telewtehu ʿalayka min asmāʾ-illahil azimul a'zamul azimu wa bihakki Allahul Ferdul Fettahu lima yuridu falikul esbahi wa cealel leyli sekenen wesh shemse wa-l- kameru husbanen zalike takdirul azizil alim. ecib billahi ʿalayka Ya Jibrīl anta wa huddamike miner ruhaniyeti wa-l- ardiyyeti bi ḥaqqi ma telewtehu ʿalayka min ismullahil azimul a'zamu wa bi ḥaqqi Allahul Cebbarul Cevvadu zul celali wa-l- ikrami ecib billahi ʿalayka Ya Semsemail anta wa huddamike miner ruhaniyeti wa-l- ardiyyeti bi ḥaqqi ma telewtehu ʿalayka min ismullahil azimul a'zamu wa bi ḥaqqi Allahush Shekurish Shakirish Shedidish Shehidil feali ala men asa minkum li hazihil asmāʾ ecib billahi ʿalayka Ya Mīkāʾīl anta wa huddamike miner ruhaniyeti wa-l- ardiyyeti bi ḥaqqi ma telewtehu ʿalayka min ismillahil azimul a'zamu wa bi hakkillahis Sabitul Vahidul Kahharu tebarakal lahu ahsenul halikun. ecib billahi ʿalayka Ya Sarfeyail anta wa huddamike miner ruhaniyeti wa-l- ardiyyeti bi ḥaqqi ma telewtehu ʿalayka min ismillahil azimul a'zamu wa bi ḥaqqi Allahuz Zahirul Batinu wa huwa bi kulli shayʾin alim. ecib Ya Anyail aleyhis salām anta wa huddamike miner ruhaniyeti wa-l- ardiyyeti bi ḥaqqi ma telewtehu ʿalayka min ismillahil azimul a'zamu wa bi ḥaqqi Allahul Habirul Halikul Alimu Haliku kulli shayʾin fa'buduhu wa huwa ala kulli shayʾin vekil. ecib Ya Kesfeyail anta wa huddamike miner ruhaniyeti wa-l- ardiyyeti bi ḥaqqi ma telewtehu ʿalayka min ismillahil azimul a'zamu wa bi ḥaqqi Allahuz zekiyyu zalikumullahi rabbekum la ilahe illa huwa kullu shayʾin halikun illa wejhehu lehul hukmu wa ileyhi turceun.

(Answer, by God's leave, O Rukyail — you and your khuddām (attendant spirits) of both the spiritual and earthly realms — by the truth of what has been recited over you of God's Greatest Name, and by the truth of God, the One, the Opener of what He wills, the Cleaver of the dawn, who made the night a repose and the sun and moon a reckoning — such is the ordaining of the Almighty, the All-Knowing. Answer, O Jibrīl — by the truth of God, the Compeller, the Generous, Lord of Majesty and Bounty. Answer, O Semsemail — by the truth of God, the Ever-Thankful, the Grateful, the Severe, the Witness, who deals with whoever among you disobeys these Names. Answer, O Mīkāʾīl — by the truth of God, the Firm, the One, the Subduer, Blessed is He, the Best of Creators. Answer, O Sarfeyail — by the truth of God, the Manifest, the Hidden, who has knowledge of all things. Answer, O Anyail, peace be upon you — by the truth of God, the All-Aware, the Creator, the All-Knowing, the Creator of all things: worship Him, for He is Guardian over all things. Answer, O Kesfeyail — by the truth of God, the Pure: that is God, your Lord; there is no god but He, the Creator of all things — everything perishes save His Face; His is the judgment, and to Him you shall return.)

Eyne Rukyail eynel Muzhib. Eyne Jibrīl eynel eyne Murreh eynel Haris eyne Semsemail eynel Ahmar Ya Muhriz eyne Mīkāʾīl eyne Burkan eyne Sarfeyail eyne Shemhuresh eynel Velideyne Anyail eynel Ebyad Ebul Hasan Zevbeah eyne Kesfeyail eyne Meymunes sehabi ecibu bi ḥaqqi ma teli ʿalaykum min ismillahil azimul a'zamu wa bi ḥaqqi sirr Fejeshin Sezhazin Allahu Ferdun Cebbarun Shekurun Sabitun Zahirun Habirun Zekiyyun elvahan elacele essaate.

(A roll call summoning each governing spirit together with his attendant or companion: Where is Rukyail, where is Muzhib? Where is Jibrīl, where are Murreh and Haris? Where is Semsemail, where is Ahmar, O Muhriz? Where is Mīkāʾīl, where is Burkan? Where is Sarfeyail, where is

Shemhuresh, where are the two sons of Velid? Where is Anyail, where is Ebyad Ebu'l-Hasan Zevbeah? Where is Kesfeyail, where is Meymunu's-Sehabi? — answer, by the truth of what has been recited over you of God's Greatest Name, and by the truth of the secret of Fejeshin Sezhazin: God, the One, the Compeller, the Ever-Thankful, the Firm, the Manifest, the All-Aware, the Pure — hasten, quickly, this very hour.) [I 606] Tāat Qasam (the Oath of Obedience) This Qasam, called the Tāat (Obedience) Qasam, has many properties and secrets, and is a majestic oath. Know its worth and its value well.
This is the Tāat Qasam:

C-d Cbr [I 607] Yf Yf Nbk+ J Bismillāhi'r-Raḥmāni'r-Raḥīm. Bismillahil hadis semi-il alimil karibil mucibid daimifi melekuti izzihil kadimil ezeliyi tuazzeze bil [I 608] kudreti ven ferade bil vahdaniyeti. The bakhūr (ritual incense) for this Qasam consists of pounded benzoin (cavi), a stick of nedd (a compound aromatic incense), Indian resin (ratīne-i hindī), sandarac (senderūs), frankincense (kundur), liquid storax (mey'atu's-sāile), red sandalwood, costus root (kust), and kākūlī oud (a prized grade of aloeswood). After pounding all of these ingredients well, you form them into pellets the size of a chickpea and dry them in the shade. Once dried, at the time of the working you burn this incense as fumigation while reciting the Qasam. In brief, you may also use the following incense instead: oud, benzoin, sandalwood, mastic, and costus root. Pound them as described above, form them into pellets the size of a chickpea, dry them in the shade, and burn them as fumigation while reciting the Qasam.

[I 610] The Khidma (service) of the Tāat Qasam The method of putting this Qasam to use is as follows: for three days, fast while keeping riyada (ascetic spiritual discipline), and after every obligatory (farz) prayer recite the Qasam seventy-two (72) times while burning the incense you have prepared. On the night of the third day, when you have recited the Qasam seventy-two (72) times, the khuddām (attendant spirits) will come and stand arrayed before you in ranks, and greet you with peace. When you finish reciting, they will say to you: "O righteous one! What do you want from us?" You then tell them that you want a covenant and a pledge from them, that they assist you in whatever you ask, in every spiritual working, whether for good or for ill, whatever you desire. They will say: "We accept what you have asked, and we will assist you whenever you call upon us." They will tell you to perform twelve rak'ahs of prayer every night, to recite the Qasam seventy-two times every day, to visit the graves of Muslims, and never to harm anyone innocent — and they will give you a green palm branch, upon which a talisman is inscribed. In this way, after this khalwa (period of ritual seclusion), you gain the right to make use of this Qasam.

After that, whenever you wish to summon them and have them come: burn your incense, hold the palm branch in your right hand above the incense, keeping it away from the flame, and recite the Qasam once (1); they will come. When they arrive, you command them as you wish.
This Tāat Qasam has many exalted khawāṣṣ (occult properties); some of them are as follows.

2. To be well received among people: write the seal on deerskin, and write the Qasam around the seal, then hang it on a branch and recite the Qasam over it seventy-two (72) times. After reciting, if you carry the seal upon you, you will witness astonishing things.

6. If you wish to learn the location of a buried treasure: take four eggs laid that same day and, burning your incense over them, write the Idmar on them. Having written it, use these eggs to terbi' (mark out the four corners of) the place you suspect. Take a brazier and set it in the middle of the ground you have marked out. Throw your incense onto the brazier, and while it smokes, stand and recite the Qasam twenty-one times; the eggs will then gather together over the suspected spot.

3. If you wish to draw a husband to his wife, or a wife to her husband, in love: write the first, second and third khawatim on a piece of cloth that has touched the maṭlūb's body. Then put oil and tar into a lamp and fit the cloth into it as a wick. Light the wick, and while it burns, recite the Qasam over it seven (7) times; you will see something that will bring you joy.

4. If you wish to draw customers to a place of business: write the seven khawatim on seven leaves, dry them in the shade, and recite the Qasam over each leaf seven (7) times. If you then hang these leaves in the place of business, its customers will multiply.
Or, write the seven khawatim on seven sheets of yellow paper, recite the Qasam over each sheet seven (7) times, and if you hang these papers in a place of business, its customers will multiply.
5. If you wish to bring a stolen item to light and learn who the thief is: write the seven khawatim, one on each of seven morsels of bread, and recite the Qasam over each morsel seven times.
[I 613] When you have finished, feed these morsels to the persons you suspect; the one who is the thief will not be able to swallow his morsel.

Or take as many cups as there are suspected persons, and recite the Qasam over each cup seven (7) times. Whichever cup belongs to the thief will turn; the cups of those who are not the thief will not turn.

6. If you wish to relieve a headache: write the seven khawatim on a shirt or on a sheet of paper. Having written them, recite the Qasam over the shirt or paper seven times; if the person suffering the headache wears this shirt, or hangs the paper on himself, the headache will pass.

Or write the seventh khātam on a piece of wood from a jumeyz (sycamore) tree, drive a nail lightly into the first hane (cell) of the khātam, and recite the Qasam once. If the pain passes, leave the nail driven in that first cell. If it does not pass, drive the nail into the second cell of the khātam and recite the Qasam once more. If it still does not pass, move the nail from cell to cell in this way until the pain is gone.

7. If you wish to relieve an eye ailment: write the seven khawatim separately on seven sheets of paper, recite the Qasam seven times over each sheet, and if the person suffering the eye pain drinks the water of one sheet each day, he will, by Allah's leave, be healed.

8. If you wish to stop the bleeding of a woman who bleeds excessively: write the seven khawatim on seven sheets of paper, and recite the Qasam over each khātam seven times. If you give the woman the water of one sheet to drink each day, her bleeding will stop and she will, by Allah's leave, be healed.

9. If you wish for an easy childbirth: write the first khātam on a sheet of paper, recite the Qasam over it seven times, and if you hang this written paper at the woman's side, she will give birth very easily.

10. If you wish for scant or withheld milk to flow: write the seven khawatim on a sheet of paper and recite the Qasam over it seven (7) times. If you then hang this paper upon the breast, the milk will flow, by Allah's leave.

11. If you wish to relieve knee pain: write the seven khawatim on seven pieces of lemon peel, recite the Qasam over each piece seven times, and if you feed one piece to the patient each day, he will, by Allah's leave, be freed from the knee pain.

[I 614] 12. If you wish to cure the disease of humma (fever): write the seven khawatim on seven sheets of paper, recite the Qasam over the papers five times, and if you fumigate the feverish person with one sheet each day, he will, by Allah's leave, be healed.

[I 674] Sebaseb Daʿwa The Sebaseb invocation is a mighty and honored invocation possessing more benefits (hasse) than can be counted.

If this invocation is recited, while in a state of cleanliness and ritual purity, over someone who is possessed by a jinn, bewitched, or afflicted by the evil eye, seven (7) days running, seven (7) times a day, then, God Almighty willing, the sick person will be healed.
The Sebaseb invocation is this:
[I 675] Types of Acquiring a Khuddām (servant Spirit)

1. Whoever wishes to be safe from poverty and misfortune should wear down his nefs (his ego, the lower self) through obedience and God-consciousness (takva) toward God Almighty. This means submitting to His commands and keeping away from what is forbidden. As far as one is able, one should eat only what is lawful and avoid what is unlawful. One should ask God Almighty for His good pleasure, for forgiveness, and for purity of heart and body. One should never grow angry at anything, should be content with God Almighty's decree, and should bear misfortunes with patience.

If you wish to attain every kind of desire and need, and to make use of a helping khadim (servant spirit): after thoroughly cleaning both the place you are in and your own body, put on seamless white clothing on a Wednesday and withdraw into a spiritual retreat (khalwa) in a clean, dark house, away from other people. Spread a clean reed mat beneath you, and place terebinth ash under the mat. On Thursday, keep the fast and break it with dried grapes. After the night prayer, perform two rak'ahs of the prayer of need. In the first and second rak'ahs, after the Fātiḥa, recite Sūrat al-Kahf. Then sit on the mat, turn toward the qibla, and recite 10,000 times:
(O Most

Subtle, O Hidden One of hidden graces, reach me with that hidden kindness of Yours by which You have sufficed all whom You have favored with it.) you say. Once you finish the recitation, a man in human form appears beside you, dressed in white, sword in hand. Do not be afraid of him! This khadim will ask you, "What is your need?" You say to him: "Give me what will make me rich, by the right of God Almighty!" The khadim will answer: "I will give it to you on this condition: you shall both eat from it and give alms from it, and you shall not do the things that are not to be done!" Then that khadim gives you a great deal of wealth. If you wish to remain his companion always, say to him: "Give me a sign to use between the two of us." He will give you a black stone. Whenever you wish to summon the khadim, light a fire and cast that stone into it. The khadim will come to you very swiftly and carry out your need. When you wish to send the khadim away, you say this:
O God, I disclaim my own power and strength (,for Yours; show me the wonders of even the least of Your kindness by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful.)
[I 676] The incense (bakhūr) for this working is Sudanese frankincense. You burn Sudanese incense while reciting. It is also of great benefit in other workings besides.

2. After cleaning your body, your clothing, and the place you are in, enter a three-day retreat while fasting and observing ascetic discipline (riyada), beginning on a Tuesday. After every obligatory prayer, recite the ʿazīma (conjuration) given below 41 times, burning sandarac, frankincense, and black gunluk resin as incense. On Friday night, spread a white sheet in the middle of the retreat room. Sit in the middle of the sheet and recite the same ʿazīma, burning the same incenses. A khuddām will appear to you in human form, the height of a hand-span, and come to your side. Do not be afraid of him! He will say to you, "What do you want from me?" You say to him: "What I want from you is that you enter my service, carry out my every command, and spend your life with me." He will say, "I hear and I obey." You then say to him: "How shall I call you?" He will teach you how to summon him.
The ʿazīma to be recited is this:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the) Compassionate — a string of invocatory names culminating in "O ("...Most Compassionate

[I 677] 3. If you wish to obtain the khuddām named Melcemeh: write the following noble wafq and hang it on the wall of your retreat room.

Write another wafq as well, and place it under your head. Enter a three-day retreat while observing riyada. Each night, encircle yourself with the recitation of Āyetu'l-kursī (the Throne Verse) and sit within that circle. Burning galbanum, goat hair, and pitch as incense, recite the following name:

One thousand five hundred (1500) times. At the start of every hundred (100) repetitions, recite the following ʿazīma once.

I adjure you, O Loving One — answer, son (of Melcemeh: make the hearts of all creation submit to me, draw them to me by the might and mercy of God, and submit and obey me, O son of Melcemeh, by the truth of Him who created me and created you, who is my Lord and your Lord, and who has power over all things.)

[I 678] You recite in this manner for three nights. On the third night, as you recite, a scream will occur. Do not be afraid! Do not answer until you have finished the name completely. This is a woman; you make an agreement with her and receive a token from her. She will come to you whenever you wish. You act according to her guidance. Keep the incense burning continuously as you recite. Do not be afraid! But the mind is like mercury — once it darts away, it can never be caught again. This is a lowly (sufli) invocation.

4. After thoroughly cleaning your body, your clothing, and the place you are in, enter a three-day retreat, remaining continuously in ritual purity, fasting, and observing riyada. After every obligatory prayer, perform eight (8) rak'ahs of prayer. In each rak'ah recite the Fātiḥa once, the Āyetu'l-kursī once, and Sūrat ad-Duhā once, giving the closing greeting after every two rak'ahs. After finishing the prayer, recite the following ʿazīma 41 times, burning plenty of sandarac incense. You continue in this manner for three days.

On the first day you hear a voice from afar. On the third day the khadim comes to you and you see him plainly. He greets you and asks, "What do you want from me?" You say to him: "I want to become your friend and brother, to learn the science of wisdom and the science of alchemy from you, and for you to place my sustenance, from lawful goods, under my pillow every night." He accepts this and enters into a mutual, sworn agreement with you. This matter is proven true.
The ʿazīma to be recited 41 times is this:
